papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting Conversion from MCI to AD Combining Multi-Modality Data and Based on Molecular Subtype (Li et al., Brain Sci. 2021)
Prediction of progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease with longitudinal and multimodal data (Ding et al., Front. Dement. 2023)

what_each_reports.P-179: Subtype-based VBpMKL classifier (MCI-CPS) on baseline FreeSurfer sMRI ROI volumes plus blood SNP and blood mRNA expression, predicting MCI-to-AD conversion within 3 years; ADNI-1 MCI n=125, 5-fold CV AUC 0.8260 (Acc 79.20%); external test on ADNI-GO/2 (n=98) AUC 0.7809. Raw classifier without subtyping 0.7849 (CV).
what_each_reports.P-168: LSTM on five visits (baseline to 24 months) of 15 neuropsychological tests plus 7 FreeSurfer MRI volumes plus demographics, predicting progression within 2 years of the 24-month index exam; ADNI-1/GO/2 participants still MCI at 24 months, n=347 (77 converters); 10-fold CV AUC 0.93 +/- 0.06. Single-visit random forest 0.90; MRI-only LSTM 0.86, MRI-only RF 0.85.

quantity_a: ROC-AUC for 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion from baseline, ADNI-1 MCI at baseline, predictors = baseline sMRI ROI volumes + peripheral-blood SNP + blood mRNA, 5-fold CV.
quantity_b: ROC-AUC for 2-year progression from a 24-month index exam, among participants still MCI at month 24 (ADNI-1/GO/2), predictors = five-visit trajectories of neuropsychological tests + MRI volumes + demographics, 10-fold CV.
incompatible_if_same: No. Neither study reports an interval that excludes the other's estimate (P-179 gives no interval; P-168's +/-0.06 is a fold SD), neither evaluates the other's method, and neither claims an ordering the other refutes. P-168's MRI-only models (0.85-0.86) sit close to P-179's 0.83, so the gap tracks the added longitudinal neuropsychological input.

gates.task: match: both T2 (MCI-to-AD conversion), but the horizons and index points differ (3 years from baseline vs 2 years from month 24).
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI in both; partial participant overlap possible (ADNI-1 MCI).
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal cross-validation for the cited figures (P-179 also reports an ADNI-GO/2 external test at 0.78).
gates.modality_family: mismatch, not waived: P-179 = structural MRI + blood genomics/transcriptomics; P-168 = neuropsychological tests + structural MRI volumes over five visits. Neither uses PET, despite the registry's MRI/PET label.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (ROC-AUC) but different endpoint horizon (3-year vs 2-year), different index point and population (baseline MCI vs participants still MCI after 24 months), and different predictor sets.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither figure reaches 0.97 (0.826 and 0.93), both flags false in the pack.
independence: Distinct author groups; both draw on ADNI, and ADNI-1 MCI participants may appear in both samples.
grounds: The predictor sets differ: P-179 uses baseline sMRI plus blood SNP and mRNA, P-168 uses five visits of neuropsychological tests plus MRI volumes, so the AUC gap confounds input with method (the C-80 precedent).
The endpoints differ: conversion within three years of baseline (P-179) against progression within two years of a 24-month index exam among those still MCI (P-168).
The modality-family gate fails (genomics vs neuropsychology added to sMRI) and no waiver is on record.
Even read as one quantity the results are not incompatible: no reported uncertainty excludes the other, and P-168's MRI-only AUC (0.86) is close to P-179's 0.83.

evidence_quotes.quote: In internal ﬁvefold cross-validation within ADNI-1, we achieved an overall AUC of 0.83 (79.20% accuracy, 81.25% sensitivity, 77.92% speciﬁcity)
Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) data and multi-omics data, including genotype data and gene expression proﬁling derived from peripheral blood samples, from 125 MCI patients
If conversion happens within three years, we deﬁne these MCI patients as having progressive MCI (P-MCI)
was developed to predict the risk of progression from MCI to AD within 2 years from the index exam (the exam at 24-month).
The longitudinal LSTM model showed superior prediction performance of MCI-to-AD progression (AUC 0.93 ± 0.06) compared to the random forest model (AUC 0.90 ± 0.09).
The LSTM model utilizing longitudinal data reached the best performance, comparing to an AUC of 0.86 when using MRI measures.

record_defects: The registry labels both papers' Modality 'MRI/PET'; neither uses PET (P-179: sMRI + blood SNP + blood mRNA; P-168: neuropsychological tests + MRI volumes + demographics).

resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (AUC); Gap magnitude 0.100 exceeds threshold', which contradicts the record's own resolution 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch'; the gap test ignores the horizon and predictor differences.
The bridging-evidence list is a generic dump of T2 ADNI papers; none is shown to identify a condition that separates these two results, so 'partially_resolved_candidate' is not supported by the note.
task_equal 'Yes' does not record that the horizons differ (3 years from baseline vs 2 years from month 24).
what_would_change_the_verdict: A comparison of the same predictor set at the same horizon and index point in both studies, with the two AUCs' uncertainty excluding each other.
